original_value: In order to realize the automatic and accurate recognition of shipwreck targets in side-scan sonar (SSS) waterfall images, a pipeline that contains feature extraction, selection, and shipwreck recognition, an AdaBoost model was constructed by sample images. Shipwreck targets are detected quickly by a nonlinear matching model, and a shipwreck recognition in SSS waterfall images are given, and according to a wide set of combinations of different types of these individual procedures, the model is able to recognize the shipwrecks accurately. Firstly, two feature-extraction methods suitable for recognizing SSS shipwreck targets from natural sea bottom images were studied. In addition to these two typical features, some commonly used features were extracted and combined as comprehensive features to characterize shipwrecks from various feature spaces. Based on Independent Component Analysis (ICA), the preferred features were selected from the comprehensive features, which avoid dimension disaster and improved the correct recognition rate. Then, the Gentle AdaBoost algorithm was studied and used for constructing the shipwreck target recognition model using sample images. Finally, a shipwreck target recognition process for the SSS waterfall image was given, and the process contains shipwreck target fast detection by a nonlinear matching model and accurate recognition by the Gentle AdaBoost recognition model. The results show that the correct recognition rate of the model for the sample image is 97.44%, while the false positive rate is 3.13% and the missing detection rate is 0. This study of a measured SSS waterfall image confirms the correctness of the recognition process and model.

result.paraphrase: To achieve automatic and accurate shipwreck target recognition in side-scan sonar (SSS) waterfall images, a sample-image-based AdaBoost model was developed within a pipeline of feature extraction, feature selection, and shipwreck recognition. Shipwreck targets are first rapidly detected by a nonlinear matching model, after which recognition is performed on SSS waterfall images; through combinations of these procedures, the model can identify shipwrecks accurately. First, two feature-extraction methods suitable for recognizing SSS shipwreck targets from natural seabed images were investigated. In addition to these two typical features, commonly used features were also extracted and merged into comprehensive features to describe shipwrecks across multiple feature spaces. Using Independent Component Analysis (ICA), the most suitable features were selected from the comprehensive set, avoiding the curse of dimensionality and improving the correct recognition rate. Next, the Gentle AdaBoost algorithm was studied and applied to build the shipwreck target recognition model from sample images. Finally, a shipwreck target recognition procedure for SSS waterfall images was presented, consisting of fast detection by a nonlinear matching model and accurate recognition by the Gentle AdaBoost recognition model. Results show that the model’s correct recognition rate on sample images is 97.44%, with a false positive rate of 3.13% and a missing detection rate of 0. The study of a measured SSS waterfall image verifies the correctness of the recognition process and the model.
